source.title: Size-free generalization bounds for convolutional neural networks

record.tranche_reason: The experiments measure how parameter count and distance from initialization relate to the train–test generalization gap, using a different measurement from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports three figure-based experimental relationships. It does not report results on random-label memorization, test-error curves past interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer or explicit-regularization comparisons, or sharpness measures.
record.test_reason: The study proves generalization bounds and measures parameter count and distance from initialization against generalization gaps. These results do not test any listed version: a flat gap does not establish declining test error beyond interpolation, and distance from initialization is not magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the experiments. The paper's main contribution is generalization bounds involving training loss, parameter count, loss Lipschitz constant, and distance from initialization. The authors describe the observed gap trends as consistent with those bounds.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies theoretical generalization bounds and measures gap correlates in a 10-layer CIFAR-10 all-convolutional model trained with dropout; it does not reproduce the interventions or settings in the listed original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The experiments sweep initial learning rates and batch sizes 32, 64, and 128; the text does not separately describe their effects.

fits_no_version.finding: In the tested CIFAR-10 convolutional networks, the generalization gap remains almost flat as parameter count increases, while distance from initialization eventually decreases with fluctuations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Widening these dropout-trained convolutional networks leaves the generalization gap approximately unchanged and eventually reduces distance from initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: The generalization gap increases with the product of parameter count and the summed layerwise operator-norm distance from initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter count times distance from initialization tracks generalization gaps in this experimental sweep.

record.problems: Experimental trends are figure-based and the supplied text gives no numerical values. Results are averaged over five random initializations; the authors note fluctuations due partly to training instability. The text does not provide a capability check or controls.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test-error behavior beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning regimes.
Large-batch performance penalties under fixed epoch budgets and their recovery through recipe changes; sweeping batch sizes alone does not establish these comparisons.
The effect of adding or removing dropout; dropout is used without a comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its relationship to generalization gaps, and its ranking against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and measuring test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains qualitative descriptions of Figures 1–3 without readable numerical plot values. No listed version receives a verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Whether test error keeps falling beyond the width needed for zero training error in the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU settings.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier performance and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch performance under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: 10-layer all-convolutional model
rows.size_stated: varying number of parameters; channels scaled in each layer
rows.operation_detail: Scaled channel counts while keeping depth and other architectural elements fixed; measured generalization gap against W
rows.measure: Generalization gap (train error minus test error) as a function of W
rows.value: The generalization gap remains almost flat with increasing W.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over five different random initializations; fluctuations are noted, but no numerical error bars are stated in the supplied text.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; figure values are not supplied.
rows.check: The flat generalization-gap trend is accurately reported, but cannot establish V2 without training and test errors and the width needed for zero training error. The gap's train-minus-test definition follows the text.

rows.subject: 10-layer all-convolutional model
rows.operation_detail: Measured the generalization gap against W multiplied by the distance from initialization
rows.measure: Generalization gap (train error minus test error) as a function of W ||K − K0||σ
rows.value: The generalization gap increases with W ||K − K0||σ.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over five different random initializations; no numerical error bars are stated in the supplied text.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; figure values are not supplied.
rows.check: The reported association is accurate but measures parameter count times distance from initialization, not V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance.

rows.subject: 10-layer all-convolutional model
rows.operation_detail: Measured distance from initialization as parameter count varied
rows.measure: ||K − K0||σ as a function of W
rows.value: The authors state that increasing W ultimately leads to a decrease in ||K − K0||σ; they also note fluctuations.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3a shows means and error bars; Figure 3b shows medians. Numerical error-bar values are not stated in the supplied text.
rows.note: The trend is described in the text, which says fluctuations partly reflect training instability; no figure values are supplied.
rows.check: The eventual decrease in distance from initialization is reported with fluctuations. This measure cannot establish any listed version; fluctuations alone do not justify a partial claim effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
